# SILICON COVERAGE POLICY — one axis per line (paiml/infra#361).
#
#   <axis-id>  <status>  <runs-on labels, comma-separated>  [job:<name glob>]  # note
#
# STATUS is one of:
#   required        this axis MUST have RUN inside its cadence window. If nothing
#                   has, silicon-nightly FAILS — a lane that silently stops
#                   covering an architecture is indistinguishable from one that
#                   never covered it.
#   pending:<issue> the axis is declared but not yet running. It does NOT fail
#                   the lane — AND IT CANNOT ROT: the preflight fails the moment a
#                   job carrying it CONCLUDES, because at that point the only
#                   thing standing between us and the coverage is this line.
#
# COVERAGE IS A RUN, NOT A RUNNER (R-5, YOGA-NIGHTLY-001 §9.2). Until 2026-09-09
# this file's question was "could a runner serve the selector?". paiml/infra#486
# registered yoga-gpu with gpu,yoga,cuda,ada and the guard instantly declared
# `x86_64-cuda-sm89` promotable — on a fleet where no job had ever carried that
# selector. A machine existing is not a test running, and promoting on it is the
# blanket exemption this ledger exists to prevent. The 4th state is now named:
# `ready` — a runner can serve it, nothing has.
#
# THE 4th COLUMN NAMES THE JOB, and it is not optional in practice. The labels
# alone are a POOL: `self-hosted,clean-room,intel` is carried by every job in the
# repo that lands on intel, including silicon-nightly's own `summary`
# aggregator — which is exactly what the first run of the run-probe matched.
# Naming the job makes the evidence specific, and it is fail-safe: rename the job
# and the axis goes UNCOVERED (red), never silently green. An axis without a 4th
# column still matches on labels alone and its verdict line is stamped
# `[labels only]`.
#
# WHY A POLICY FILE AND NOT A MATRIX. aprender's correctness is silicon-dependent
# — SIMD paths, CUDA kernels, arch intrinsics, float behaviour — and the axes we
# do NOT cover are the interesting number. A `matrix:` lists what runs; this
# lists what SHOULD run and makes the gap a value rather than an absence.
#
# The gap is real and was widened deliberately: paiml/aprender#2740 makes
# cuda-nightly gx10-only because its x86_64 GPU leg ran on lambda-labs, which
# must never be a CI host (paiml/infra#359). sm_89 was the STABLE reference and
# sm_121 the higher-risk target with a history of JIT bugs; we now gate only the
# risky one. `x86_64-cuda-sm89` below is that hole, named — and being closed:
# yoga is registered (paiml/infra#486) and the `ada-yoga` leg of cuda-nightly.yml
# is what will flip this line from pending to required (R-4, then R-5 step 9).

x86_64-cpu          required        self-hosted,clean-room,intel            job:x86_64-cpu
aarch64-cuda-sm121  required        self-hosted,gpu,gx10,cuda,blackwell     job:aarch64-cuda-sm121

# ── declared, not yet runnable ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Each of these has `runner-register` make targets in paiml/infra. Standing one
# up needs the paiml/infra#352 treatment: an opt-in label, never the default
# pool, and a guard that nothing can select it implicitly.
#
# x86_64-cuda-sm89 is the one in motion: yoga-gpu is REGISTERED and online, so
# this axis reads `ready` rather than `deferred`. It promotes to `required` when
# the `ada-yoga` leg has actually run — not before (N-1).
x86_64-cuda-sm89    pending:361     self-hosted,gpu,yoga,cuda,ada           job:ada-yoga*
aarch64-cuda-sm87   pending:361     self-hosted,gpu,jetson,cuda,orin        job:aarch64-cuda-sm87
aarch64-macos       pending:361     self-hosted,mini,macos,arm64            job:aarch64-macos
